source.title: Vision-Language Asymmetry in Bistable Image Captioning

record.tranche_reason: The study measures co-activation of SAE feature pools for paired interpretations of ambiguous images, not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether such neuron responses share a feature.
record.gate_note: The reported SAE pool co-activation results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version: they concern feature-pool representations, not individual-neuron polysemanticity or a shared feature explaining a mixed-response neuron. Caption steering results measure commitment in generated captions, not polysemanticity, so they are not rows. Cited findings from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study trains a TopK SAE on CLIP layer 22 of LLaVA-1.6-7B. It uses SAE features, a tool motivated by neurons not being monosemantic, to find aspect-specific feature pools for bistable images. It never measures individual neurons, how many neurons are polysemantic, or what causes polysemanticity. Its 'superposition' means both interpretation-specific feature pools are active on one image. That is a different sense from features packed into fewer neurons. None of its results bear on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add a methodological point: rank statistics on sparse TopK SAE outputs need tie-corrected ranking. Without it, an earlier pass produced about 10–14k phantom B-preferring features per group. They also report that steering at layer 22 flips duck–rabbit captions (33% rabbit) but cannot flip young/old captions. From this they place commitment downstream of the vision tower.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a TopK SAE on CLIP layer-22 activations, identifies aspect-specific feature pools, and tests co-activation and causal steering on bistable-image captions; it does not use a single-neuron polysemanticity measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The co-activation share varies by stimulus group, from 1/4 for Schroeder stairs to 13/14 for Necker cubes; the authors flag the small pure-B control set for Schroeder stairs.

fits_no_version.finding: At CLIP layer 22, the duck-pool and rabbit-pool SAE features (and other aspect pairs) were both above opposite-control thresholds for 50/69 bistable stimuli. Per group: duck rabbit 12/12, face vase 7/16, hidden face 10/15, young old woman 7/8, schroeder stairs 1/4, necker cube 13/14.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In LLaVA-1.6-7B's vision tower, SAE features for both interpretations of a bistable image are often co-active, even when captions commit to one interpretation.

record.code_released: not stated; code, configs, and per-stimulus result tables are said to be released upon acceptance
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The representational conclusion is limited to one VLM and one SAE training run. The paper notes that the Schroeder-stairs pure-B control set is small (n = 8), and that cross-model, cross-SAE, random-feature, and permuted-aspect baselines remain for future work. The results do not measure individual-neuron responses.
record.rows_left_out: Phase 4 steering results are not included: their measure is caption commitment under injected steering, not neuron polysemanticity or the feature-pool co-activation finding recorded here.

untested.parts: No individual neurons in image classifiers are examined, only SAE features on CLIP layer 22.
No language-model MLP neurons are analysed.
Does not test whether neurons are polysemantic because features outnumber neurons. The word 'superposition' is used for co-activation of interpretation pools.
Initialization, regularization and training noise are not studied.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures or regularization.
No canonical polysemantic neuron is revisited.
The tie-ranking artifact concerns AUROC selection of SAE features, not whether neurons count as polysemantic.

record.verdict_notes: The record called the study cites_only/T6, but the paper does not cite Zoom In or SoLU. It relies on SAEs as a tool (Pach et al., 'monosemantic features'), so uses_without_test/T4 fits better; either way no version is tested. The terminology clash matters: 'superposition' here means co-active interpretation pools, not the superposition hypothesis, so these results must not be read as V3 evidence. Phase 4 steering was correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure individual neurons in image classifiers or test whether single neurons respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
No language-model MLP neurons, tokens, or contexts are examined.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than there are neurons.
Initialization, regularization, training noise, and capacity relative to feature count are not tested as causes of neuron polysemanticity.
The study does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization for their effects on the share of polysemantic neurons.
The study does not revisit a canonical mixed-response neuron or test whether its responses share one feature or related jobs.
It discusses a ranking artifact in sparse SAE outputs, but does not test how activation-range choices or explanation scores change whether neurons count as polysemantic.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.6-Vicuna-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured simultaneous activation of aspect-specific SAE feature pools at CLIP layer 22 on bistable stimuli.

conditions.value: all six groups; 69 stimuli with both pools available

rows.measure: Stimuli classified as superposition when both aspect pools exceeded their opposite-aspect-control thresholds
rows.baseline: Per-pool threshold was the median activation on opposite-aspect controls; numeric thresholds not stated
rows.note: This is a feature-pool measurement, not a measurement of individual neurons.
rows.check: Link to 'none' is correct. The measure is co-activation of two 15-feature SAE pools, not neuron polysemanticity. The paper's 'superposition' label does not mean the superposition hypothesis of V3, so the row must not be linked to V3.
